free_tier.stated: Unlimited storage for public, non-embeddable videos; 3 GB total for embeddable and non-public videos. This is a 2024-onwards rewrite of the old '500 MB/week' rule. The weekly quota now applies only to legacy paid Plus/Pro accounts, not Free.

retention.stated: The killer is not quota, it is that Vimeo deletes exactly the thing you want to store: 'your source file will be permanently deleted if you are a Free or Basic member'

egress.terms: Unlimited bandwidth for public non-embeddable videos; 1 TB/month for embeddable and non-public. No per-GB charge on Free.

record.tooling: The yt-dlp tool includes a Vimeo extractor that requires authentication cookies for protected content. Vimeo API v3 exposes `/me/videos`, but direct binary download links require paid subscriptions.
record.chaining: Unlimited public videos x unlimited free accounts. In principle unbounded capacity at zero cost. The only thing stopping it is the original-file problem below.
record.limits_note: ~200 GB per file advised for a successful upload, and no video longer than 24 hours. That 200 GB/file is genuinely large.
record.reliability_note: The killer is not quota, it is that Vimeo deletes exactly the thing you want to store: 'your source file will be permanently deleted if you are a Free or Basic member'. Free accounts also cannot enable downloads at all, so there is no supported retrieval path.
